note: MPP maps x402 headers onto Payment authentication and x402 exact onto charge; upto and batch-settlement are comparable to sessions. mppx's EVM charge has offered both protocols on one route since 0.6.29 (2026-06-02), 0.9.0 added dual MPP and x402 framework wrappers, and the mppx client prefers the Payment challenge. Tempo also runs an x402 facilitator (live by 2026-11-19, with a tempoX402() helper in mppx 0.21.1) that takes USDC on Base and pays sellers in OUSD on Tempo; buyers pay Tempo's deposit address, so sellers rely on Tempo for the payout.

Both are HTTP 402 payment protocols; MPP's comparison page, written by its authors, recommends MPP by default. Stripe co-authors MPP and sits on the x402 TSC, and Tempo, MPP's other co-author, runs an x402 facilitator.
No protocol cross-reference; the shared component is Stripe Shared Payment Tokens, which the stripe method carries and Stripe also uses for agentic checkout.

The Visa-authored card method lets a client add TAP signature headers (in the spec since 2026-03-18); Visa says the card spec and SDK are built on VIC and TAP; mppx checks TAP signatures outside the spec, as request attestation until 0.16.0 (2026-10-28) and as a per-route identity verifier and prover since.

Tempo's statement only: in Mastercard's 2026-06-10 AP4M release Tempo says it is excited to work with Mastercard on MPP compatibility. Mastercard makes no MPP claim and has no MPP method spec, and its 2026-10-20 brief opening AP4M Early Access says AP4M builds on x402 and names no MPP, Tempo or Stripe.

Complementary in principle (AP2 carries user authorization evidence, MPP settles payment) but no specification binds them and neither repository mentions the other. In AP2, MPP means Merchant Payment Processor.

An SDK link, not a specification link: since mppx 0.20.0 (2026-11-16) MPP's reference SDK ships an ERC-8004 identity provider (mppx/extensions/identity/erc8004). The agent signs requests with its wallet and sends Agent-Id and Agent-Signature; the server checks that the wallet the Identity Registry names for the agent (on Tempo mainnet by default) signed the request or the agent's tempo charge. No MPP draft specifies this; draft-payment-discovery-01 only cites ERC-8004 as prior art.
